+"""Shared outbound-URL policy for server-side requests to remote instances.
+
+Remote-instance addresses are operator-supplied and later dereferenced by the
+sync worker, so they must be constrained to public HTTP(S) destinations to
+avoid server-side request forgery against internal or cloud-metadata services.
+
+The policy is applied at two points:
+
+* :func:`validate_remote_instance_url` runs when an address is stored. It is a
+  syntactic HTTP(S) check plus a boundary check for hosts given as IP literals.
+  DNS is deliberately not resolved here, so a target that is temporarily
+  unreachable can still be configured.
+* :func:`safe_get` runs at request time. It resolves the host, rejects any
+  non-public address, and follows redirects manually so a 3xx pointing at an
+  internal host is rejected rather than followed.
+"""
+
+import ipaddress
+import re
+import socket
+from typing import Any
+from urllib.parse import urljoin, urlparse
+
+import requests
+
+ALLOWED_SCHEMES = {"http", "https"}
+MAX_REDIRECTS = 5
+
+# scheme + host, no whitespace; mirrors the historical remote-instance check.
+_URL_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^https?://[^\s/$.?#].[^\s]*$", re.IGNORECASE)
+
+
+class UnsafeRemoteURLError(ValueError):
+    """A remote URL is malformed or resolves to a non-public host.
+
+    Subclasses ``ValueError`` so existing model-validation error handling keeps
+    working unchanged.
+    """
+
+
+def _is_public_ip(ip: str) -> bool:
+    """Return True only for globally routable unicast addresses."""
+    addr = ipaddress.ip_address(ip)
+    return not (
+        addr.is_private
+        or addr.is_loopback
+        or addr.is_link_local
+        or addr.is_multicast
+        or addr.is_reserved
+        or addr.is_unspecified
+    )
+
+
+def _parse(url: str) -> Any:
+    """Parse and syntactically validate an HTTP(S) URL with a host."""
+    if not _URL_PATTERN.match(url or ""):
+        raise UnsafeRemoteURLError("Invalid URL format for address.")
+    parsed = urlparse(url)
+    if parsed.scheme.lower() not in ALLOWED_SCHEMES:
+        raise UnsafeRemoteURLError("Only http(s) URLs are allowed.")
+    if not parsed.hostname:
+        raise UnsafeRemoteURLError("URL has no host.")
+    return parsed
+
+
+def validate_remote_instance_url(url: str) -> str:
+    """Validate an address at storage time.
+
+    Enforces the HTTP(S) syntax and, when the host is an IP literal, blocks
+    private, loopback, link-local, multicast, reserved and unspecified ranges.
+    Hostnames are resolved and re-checked later, at request time.
+    """
+    parsed = _parse(url)
+    host = parsed.hostname
+    try:
+        ipaddress.ip_address(host)
+    except ValueError:
+        return url  # hostname, not an IP literal: checked at request time
+    if not _is_public_ip(host):
+        raise UnsafeRemoteURLError(
+            "Address must not point to a private, loopback or link-local host."
+        )
+    return url
+
+
+def _assert_public_host(host: str) -> None:
+    """Resolve host and raise if any resolved address is non-public."""
+    try:
+        infos = socket.getaddrinfo(host, None)
+    except socket.gaierror as exc:
+        raise UnsafeRemoteURLError(f"Cannot resolve host {host!r}: {exc}")
+    for info in infos:
+        ip = str(info[4][0])
+        if not _is_public_ip(ip):
+            raise UnsafeRemoteURLError(
+                f"Host {host!r} resolves to non-public address {ip}."
+            )
+
+
+def safe_get(
+    url: str,
+    *,
+    params: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
+    headers: dict[str, str] | None = None,
+    timeout: Any = None,
+) -> requests.Response:
+    """GET a remote URL under the outbound-request policy.
+
+    The initial URL and every redirect hop are validated and their host
+    resolved to public addresses before the request is issued; redirects are
+    followed manually (up to :data:`MAX_REDIRECTS`) so a 3xx pointing at a
+    private, loopback or link-local host is rejected instead of followed.
+
+    Raises :class:`UnsafeRemoteURLError` for a disallowed destination.
+
+    Note: ``requests`` re-resolves the host when it opens the connection, so
+    this does not fully close a DNS-rebinding race; it does block static
+    internal hostnames, IP literals and cloud-metadata endpoints, which is the
+    exposure being addressed.
+    """
+    next_url = url
+    next_params = params
+    for _ in range(MAX_REDIRECTS + 1):
+        parsed = _parse(next_url)
+        _assert_public_host(parsed.hostname)
+        resp = requests.get(
+            next_url,
+            params=next_params,
+            headers=headers,
+            timeout=timeout,
+            allow_redirects=False,
+        )
+        if resp.is_redirect or resp.is_permanent_redirect:
+            location = resp.headers.get("Location")
+            if not location:
+                return resp
+            # The query string is already baked into the redirect target.
+            next_url = urljoin(next_url, location)
+            next_params = None
+            continue
+        return resp
+    raise UnsafeRemoteURLError(f"Too many redirects while fetching {url!r}.")
